note: Generated by test/gen-sexpr-vectors.sc from (igropyr sexpr) -- the authority for this wire format.  Do not hand-edit.  The read probes' inputs are chosen by the generator; every VERDICT here, and every wire string in the write groups, is what that implementation produced. Wire text is base64 of its UTF-8 bytes, except where an entry is too long to carry literally: those appear as a *_rule object (prefix, repeated character, count, suffix) that rebuilds the text exactly.
anchors_are: type x spelling-branch over the whole value model.  Each entry carries a spec -- a prefix token program whose payloads are all decimal integers and whose text is UTF-8 bytes -- and the wire the authority produces for the value that spec denotes.  A consumer builds the value from the spec WITHOUT its own codec and asserts both directions against the wire; that is what a fixed-point round trip cannot ask.  direction=both means the authority also emits this exact wire for the value; direction=read means the wire is an accepted spelling the writer does not itself produce.  Downstream tests are expected to pin the branch names, so a branch cannot quietly leave.  Every entry carries the atom its value is, and a nesting entry also the position it places it in, so a branch name is a claim checked against the decoded value as far as the label reaches. It does not reach everywhere: where two branches share a label (integer/positive and integer/negative are both small-integer, flonum/half and flonum/repeating both flonum) their names are conventions, and swapping such a pair's values and wires would not be detected.  The section is additive: a consumer that does not want it can ignore it.
spec_corpus_is: Programs in the spec language that every reader of it must refuse (malformed) and must accept (wellformed).  The generator runs both against its own reader before writing this file; the consumers run both against theirs.  The wellformed list is not decoration: a reader that refused everything would satisfy the malformed list perfectly.
